findings.quote: Machine facts: `npx supabase` 2.x is available; `supabase gen types typescript --db-url …` talks to Postgres directly and needs no Docker.
findings.problem: The Supabase CLI implements `gen types --db-url` by running the postgres-meta image in Docker (only `--project-id`/`--linked` go over HTTP). The skeleton says Docker is unavailable on the agents' machines, so `scripts/db/gen-types.sh` as written cannot run locally, `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` is never produced, and the CI drift step (which does have Docker) would generate a file the agent cannot reproduce. The prompt's only fallback is 'pin npx supabase@<version> or document the flag', which does not remove the Docker dependency.
findings.fix: Replace the 'Machine facts' bullet with: 'Verify first: `npx supabase gen types typescript --db-url "$DATABASE_URL" --schema public | head -3`. If the CLI reports that Docker is required (it runs postgres-meta in a container for `--db-url`), do NOT use the CLI: `gen-types.sh` starts the same generator without Docker — `PG_META_DB_URL="$URL" PG_META_PORT=<free port> npx -y @supabase/postgres-meta@<pinned exact version> &`, wait for `curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health`, then `curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/generators/typescript?included_schemas=public&detect_one_to_one_relationships=true" > packages/db/src/database.types.ts`, kill the server. Use this path unconditionally (also in CI) so output is byte-identical everywhere; pin the postgres-meta version in the script and in HANDOFF version pins.' Keep the empty-output/`export type Database` guard. Add to Verify: `bash scripts/db/gen-types.sh` twice → `git diff --exit-code packages/db/src/database.types.ts` clean, with no Docker daemon running.

findings.quote: add, idempotently, `alter role service_role bypassrls;` (as on Supabase; `login_service()` relies on it) and `alter table storage.objects enable row level security;`
findings.problem: G2's shim grants only `select` on `storage.buckets`/`storage.objects` to `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role`. Step 1.4b test 07(b) does `insert into storage.objects … as uploader` (must succeed via `ca_storage_insert`), `update`/`delete` as uploader (must return 0 rows because there is no policy, not 42501 because there is no privilege) and `login_service()` deletes the row. Without table privileges every one of those fails with 42501 before the policies are exercised, and the 'no update/delete policy' assertion is untestable. Supabase grants `all` on `storage.objects` to these roles.
findings.fix: Extend Build item 6 with a third idempotent shim tweak: `grant select, insert, update, delete on storage.objects, storage.buckets to authenticated, service_role;` (Supabase grants these; the `ca_storage_*` policies and the absence of update/delete policies do the filtering). Add to 09_grants item (5): `has_table_privilege('authenticated','storage.objects','insert')` true, and mention in the HANDOFF shim note.

findings.quote: Every test file starts with `\set ON_ERROR_STOP on` and `begin;` and ends with `rollback;` so nothing persists.
findings.problem: `\set` is a psql meta-command; DESIGN §12 says the test files run verbatim in the hosted SQL editor and step 1.5's runbook tells the founder to paste them. The mandated header makes every file fail on paste with a syntax error, and 1.5 documents only 08's `\i` as the exception. `test.sh` already passes `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, so the header is redundant.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Every test file is plain SQL: it starts with `begin;` and ends with `rollback;` (test.sh supplies `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`; never put psql meta-commands in a test except the documented `\i` in 08). Files must paste unchanged into the hosted SQL editor.' Apply the same rule in the Done-when bullet about helpers/tests.

findings.quote: Fixture builders, `security definer set search_path = ''` (they bypass RLS whatever role the test currently runs as)
findings.problem: Bypassing RLS is not enough: 1.3a's trigger guards (`guard_persons_columns`, `guard_household_privacy_columns`, `force_event_pending`, `stamp_response_scope`, `assert_same_org`) fire regardless of role and read `auth.uid()`. The prompt never says under which identity fixtures are built (logged out = null uid, or as a super admin), nor whether 1.3a's guards treat a null uid as trusted. If they do not, `make_person(... congregation_status => 'member')` and the 01_tenancy content inserts (approved events, published content 'in each org') are rejected or silently rewritten (event forced to pending), and two agents would build incompatible harnesses. The same gap hits 1.4b (every file) and 1.5 (which hard-codes 'claims = seed super admin').
findings.fix: Add to Build item 7 a paragraph: 'Identity for fixtures: builders and direct content inserts are executed while logged out (`app_test.logout()` — role `churchapp_owner`, `auth.uid()` null). Read 1.3a's guard functions first: if any guard rejects or rewrites rows when `auth.uid()` is null, do not weaken the guard — instead make every builder set the claims to a per-run super admin for the duration of the call (`app_test.make_super()` inserts a user + `super_admins` row; builders `perform set_config('request.jwt.claims', …super…, true)` and restore the previous value on exit). State the chosen convention in the helpers.sql header and in HANDOFF (steps 1.4b and 1.5 rely on it).' In item 9, say explicitly that the per-org content rows (sermon, announcement, bulletin, document, event, audience group) are inserted through that same convention, and that the approved event must be verified to stay `approved`.

findings.quote: `local-up.sh` skips the shim on an existing database, so drop and recreate yours once (`dropdb` through `.local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL`, then `local-up.sh`); CI starts fresh.
findings.problem: The step's verification (and 1.4b's and 1.5's standing sequence) silently fails on any machine whose `churchapp` database predates this step, because `local-up.sh` never re-applies the shim; the founder's other agents will hit this at 1.4b/1.5 with no instruction. 'dropdb through PG_SUPER_URL' is also not an executable command.
findings.fix: Replace item 6's last sentence with: 'Make the tweak reach existing databases: change `scripts/db/local-up.sh` so that it always applies `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` (the shim is fully idempotent) instead of skipping it when `auth.uid()` exists — a one-line change; keep the fast-path for an already-running cluster. Record the change in HANDOFF. (If you prefer not to touch local-up.sh: `psql "$(cat .local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL)" -c "drop database churchapp"` then `bash scripts/db/local-up.sh`.)' Update the first Verify bullet accordingly (drop the vague `dropdb`-then-local-up wording; assert `select rolbypassrls from pg_roles where rolname = 'service_role'` → `t` after a plain `local-up.sh` on the existing database).

findings.quote: Work inside `9999_init.sql` sections (8)–(11), `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` (one local-only tweak), `supabase/tests/helpers.sql`, `supabase/tests/rls/{01_tenancy,08_rerunnable,09_grants}.sql`, `scripts/db/test.sh`
findings.problem: Orchestrator decision 13 caps a step at one large SQL section. This step contains the full ~95-policy catalogue plus grants plus storage (one large section) AND a second substantial SQL body (helpers.sql ≈ 17 functions, three multi-assertion test files, test.sh rewrite). If the session runs out mid-harness the repo is left with policies that no test exercises and 1.4b cannot start.

Record the choice in notes.

findings.quote: `app_test.login(uid uuid)` (`execute 'set local role authenticated'` then `set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', uid, 'role', 'authenticated', 'email', <profiles.email>)::text, true)`)
findings.problem: In the stated order the email lookup runs after `set role authenticated` with no claims yet set, so the `profiles` policy returns nothing (and `login` is invoker, so RLS applies). Two agents would resolve this differently.
findings.fix: Reorder: 'read the email from `auth.users` (or `profiles`) into a variable BEFORE `set local role`, then switch role, then `set_config`'. Also state that `login()` raises when the uid does not exist.

findings.quote: run each `supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` in name order with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -f` capturing output to a scratch log
findings.problem: `raise notice 'ok: …'` and error text go to stderr; capturing only stdout loses the 'last 20 log lines on failure' the prompt promises.
findings.fix: Write `… -q -f "$f" > "$log" 2>&1` and say the scratch log lives under the session's scratchpad directory, never `/tmp`.

findings.quote: every public table has `relrowsecurity` true and `relforcerowsecurity` false
findings.problem: `pg_class` rows for views (the three `directory_*` views are in `public`) have `relrowsecurity = false`; an unqualified check fails or is silently narrowed differently by each agent.
findings.fix: Write 'every `pg_class` row in schema `public` with `relkind in ('r','p')` has …'. Same for the 'no 42P17' loop in 01_tenancy: iterate `pg_tables`, not `information_schema.tables`, so views are excluded.

The step's commit_message is the last commit.'

findings.quote: load the file with `\set fixture `cat packages/domain/fixtures/persons.json`` and `jsonb_array_elements((:'fixture')::jsonb -> 'persons')`
findings.problem: A psql backtick expansion is psql-only and shell-dependent; the file cannot run in the hosted SQL editor, contradicting DESIGN §12 and 1.5's runbook, which names only 08's `\i` as an exception.

findings.quote: `submit_audience_group_id` = the `men` group → a female member's insert → 42501

findings.quote: wrong password → `wrong_password` and `view_count` still 0; 9 more wrong attempts → the 11th call (any password) → `rate_limited`
findings.problem: Whether the initial `needs_password` call (null password) counts as a failure is not defined by DESIGN or 1.3b; if it does, the lock arrives one call earlier and the assertion is wrong by one.
findings.fix: State: 'Only calls that return `wrong_password` count as failures (a `needs_password` probe does not); if 1.3b counts the probe, assert the lock at the 10th failing call and record it in HANDOFF for step 3.4.'

findings.quote: grep confirms every sentence has one (some live in 1.4a's files)

findings.quote: (b) inserts auth users with FIXED uuids … (c) FIRST sets the JWT claims to the seed super admin
findings.problem: `app.is_super_admin()` reads `public.super_admins`; unless that row is inserted before the claims are set and before the first guarded insert, every 'runs as super admin' guard sees an ordinary user and rejects the seed. The prompt lists the `super_admins` row only under 'Users' without ordering it.
findings.fix: Make the order explicit in item 1: '(b) insert the seed auth users; (b2) insert the `super_admins` row for `seed-super`; (c) set the claims to `seed-super` and assert `app.is_super_admin()` is true before inserting anything else (raise if not).' Also say what to do if 1.3a's guards do not honour super admins (then run the seed under the per-org `admin` claims instead, switching per org).

findings.quote: Sanity-assert the enum block: `Database['public']['Enums']['permission_key']` lists the 12 keys in PLAN §4 order.
findings.problem: No command is given; the generator emits enums in definition order, which the agent cannot 'assert' without a concrete check, and the enum-parity type test belongs to 1.7.
findings.fix: Give the check: `node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('packages/db/src/database.types.ts','utf8');const m=s.match(/permission_key:\s*((?:\s*\|?\s*\"[a-z_.]+\")+)/);const keys=[...m[1].matchAll(/\"([a-z_.]+)\"/g)].map(x=>x[1]);if(keys.length!==12)process.exit(1);console.log(keys.join(','))"` → prints the 12 keys in PLAN §4 order.
